claims.text: The studied system is a single-crystal FeNiCrCoCu high-entropy-alloy coating on a single-crystal Cu matrix.
The initial coating is a defect-rich FCC crystal containing measurable dislocations and stacking faults.
Nanoindentation is performed to a depth of 30 Å at 10 m/s and at 300, 600, 900, and 1200 K.
Above 900 K, stacking faults and dislocations rapidly annihilate through thermally activated climb and cross-slip.
The annihilation of dislocations produces dislocation starvation above 900 K.
Localized amorphization begins in the indentation contact zone when thermal disorder overwhelms lattice stability.
The combined dislocation starvation and amorphization eliminate strain-hardening capacity.
Loss of strain hardening promotes shear localization and severe plastic deformation.
Above 900 K, deformation changes from dislocation-mediated plasticity to a thermally softened, amorphous-like regime.
This microstructural transition sharply reduces hardness, increases friction, and destroys wear resistance.
Above 900 K, hardness and wear resistance will fall by more than 50% relative to their values at 600 K.
The friction coefficient will spike above 900 K.
HCP atom count will first rise transiently and then fall as amorphization becomes dominant.
Dislocation line length will decrease sharply above 900 K because of dislocation annihilation.
At 600 K, dislocation density decreases slightly and this increases the elastic modulus while crystalline order and moderate wear resistance are retained.
At lower strain rates or in polycrystalline samples, grain-boundary effects dominate, so the proposed mechanism does not apply.
A transient HCP-count peak followed by a drop, together with decreasing dislocation line length, distinguishes disorder-driven thermal softening from mechanical annealing.
Mechanical annealing would instead produce a persistently low HCP count and reduced dislocation line length without amorphization signatures.
A correlation between amorphization onset and the friction spike would confirm the proposed mechanism.
